semantic_fragments.content: Clause 5.4 requires the MANUFACTURER to identify and describe the reasonably foreseeable HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS associated with the identified HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS. The description of each identified HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO shall include all TASKS and their sequences as well as the SEVERITY of the associated HARM. The results of this identification shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

Clause 5.5 requires the MANUFACTURER to select the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS to be included in the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION. Selection options include: all HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS; a subset based on SEVERITY of potential HARM that could be caused by USE ERROR (e.g. for which medical intervention would be needed); or a subset based on SEVERITY of potential HARM and other circumstances specific to the MEDICAL DEVICE and the MANUFACTURER. A summary of any selection scheme, the rationale for its use and the results of applying it shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

Clause 5.6 requires the MANUFACTURER to establish and maintain a USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION. The specification shall consider: the USE SPECIFICATION (see 5.1); the known or foreseeable USE ERRORS associated with the MEDICAL DEVICE (see 5.2); and the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS (see 5.4). The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall include: testable technical requirements relevant to the USER INTERFACE, including requirements for parts associated with selected RISK CONTROL measures; an indication as to whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is required; and an indication as to whether MEDICAL DEVICE-specific training is required. The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE and may be integrated into other specifications.

Clause 5.7.1 specifies that the USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan shall: a) document the objective and identify the method of any planned FORMATIVE EVALUATIONS and SUMMATIVE EVALUATIONS; b) if USABILITY TESTS are employed, document which USER GROUPS are intended to be included in the test, document the test environment and other conditions of use based on the USE SPECIFICATION, specify whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is provided during the test, and specify whether MEDICAL DEVICE-specific training is provided prior to the test and the minimum elapsed time between training and the beginning of the test. USER INTERFACE EVALUATION methods may be quantitative or qualitative and may be performed in a laboratory setting, simulated USE ENVIRONMENT or actual USE ENVIRONMENT. The plan may be integrated into other plans and shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.
